title: MIG-slice OOM playbook - scratch
content:
Problem sketch:
- Reproducer: model serving container on a MIG 3g.20gb slice (A100-MIG) intermittently fails during batch inference with CUDA OOM, even though nvidia-smi shows ~2-4GB free at the time. Failures started after host driver bump from 525.x -> 535.x and container base updated to ubuntu 22.04 + CUDA 12.1 libs.

Symptoms observed (notes and snippets):
- Torch error (from logs):
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.65 GiB (GPU 0; 19.53 GiB total capacity; 14.02 GiB already allocated; 255.00 MiB free; 5.21 GiB cached)
  -- this looked odd because nvidia-smi inside container: 19.53 GiB total vs MIG slice expected 20GB, but the "already allocated" numbers don't match process RSS.

- nvidia-smi (host):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  | GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB MIG 3g.20gb                                     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Processes:                                                                  |
  |  GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
  |    0    3    0      22415      C   python                           12132MiB |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  - Host shows ~12GB used by python process, leaving ~8GB free. But inside container the process sees less free memory (OOM).

- dmesg around time of failure: (host)
  [  8421.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 22415 (python) total-vm:81920000kB, anon-rss:12345678kB, file-rss:0kB
  -> kernel OOM killer triggered inside MIG partition.

- NVML reports removed/unknown when the container is launched with the old nvidia-container-runtime and host driver mismatch:
  NVML Error: Driver/library version mismatch

What I tried (commands & config tried):
- Environment introspection:
  $ nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
  $ ls -l /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so*
  $ readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
  Observed: container had libcuda.so.1 coming from CUDA12.1 toolkit (/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64) while host driver was 535.x. There were two different SONAMEs resolved during runtime (libcuda.so.1 -> libcuda.so.535.54.03). Suspect inconsistent loader ordering.

- Run with LD_DEBUG=libs to confirm which libcuda is being loaded (inside container). Confirmed container loader picks up the toolkit libcuda first, then the driver shim. That can cause NVML to return mismatched versions.

- Repro attempts with different docker invocation:
  # baseline that reproduces
  docker run --gpus 'device=0' --rm -it --ipc=host my-serving-image:canary /bin/bash -c "python serve.py --batch-size 24"

  # try mapping host libs
  docker run --gpus all --env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/nvidia/lib:/usr/local/nvidia/lib64 --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/host-lib -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 --rm -it my-serving-image:canary bash

  # explicit LD_PRELOAD to force host libcuda (temporary test)
  LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 python serve.py --batch-size 24
  -> temporarily eliminated NVML mismatch but still saw sporadic OOMs after 10-30 mins.

- Torch/CUDA fragmentation mitigations tried:
  - Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to reduce fragmentation.
  - torch.cuda.empty_cache() in between batches.
  - Use torch.autocast for AMP and reduced batch_size.
  Observed: fragmentation reduced but OOM still happens under peak concurrency.

- NCCL / multi-process checks:
  - Disabled NCCL for a single-worker test (set environment NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0). No change.

- MIG-specific checks:
  - Checked host MIG assignment: nvidia-smi mig -lgi shows GI 3 in use and the container is running inside that GI+CI mapping.
  - Confirmed no cross-GI interference on host by running stress tests on a different GI concurrently; memory accounting remained isolated.

- cgroups / kubernetes integration notes:
  - On k8s (gke/redwood cluster) the pod had resource limits set for memory but not GPU memory obviously. Confirmed kubelet / nvidia device plugin v0.12 is used.
  - Found kernel messages (from node) indicating "cgroup memory limit exceeded" for the container at similar timestamps. Could be host OOM due to another process spiking.

Hypotheses (sorted roughly high->low prob):
1) Driver/toolkit library mismatch at loader time causes NVML and driver to disagree on resident memory accounting; kernel ends up killing process inside MIG slice even though userland thought memory was free (race between allocation and kernel accounting).
2) Fragmentation amplified by FP16+AMP + continuous batching + TORCH caching behavior on MIG slices (smaller slice = less ability to satisfy large contiguous allocations) -> intermittent large allocation fails though aggregate free memory seems sufficient.
3) A host-level memory spike (other guest or host daemon) triggers kernel OOM in the slice despite lib reporting free pages (accounting timing issue).
4) A subtle kernel/driver bug introduced in 535.x with MIG accounting under cgroups / containers (observed after driver bump).

Minimal repro (attempt):
- python snippet to reproduce quickly (inside same container):
  import torch
  torch.cuda.init()
  a = []
  for i in range(100):
      try:
          a.append(torch.empty((1024,1024,256), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda'))
      except Exception as e:
          print('alloc fail at step', i, e)
          break
  # wait and check nvidia-smi, dmesg

Notes from kernel logs when reproducible locally:
- dmesg shows: "nv-hostengine: migrate: failed to allocate pages for mig instance" and then "nvidia: GPU fault: Reason: OOM"

What gave temporary relief:
- Forcing container to use host libcuda (LD_PRELOAD) and restarting nvidia-persistenced reduced NVML/driver mismatch errors.
- Reducing batch-size from 24 -> 12 eliminated OOMs for >24 hours (practical mitigation).
- TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF helped reduce fragmentation-related small alloc fails.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Reproduce consistently on bare-metal host with same driver/toolkit combo. If reproducible, file bug with NVIDIA including dmesg, driver version, MIG config.
- [ ] Re-run with driver pinned to previous stable (525.x) on one node to validate regression.
- [ ] Add a small watchdog in serve.py to catch allocation exceptions and fall back to smaller batch/FP32 fallback automatically.
- [ ] Try running the same workload with CUDA 12.0 toolkit libs in container (avoid toolkit-driver mismatch).
- [ ] Collect full LD_DEBUG=libs logs and attach to INC-2025-2374 and PR #842 for visibility.
- [ ] Instrument nvml.smi to poll memory every 200ms from host and inside container to detect timing discrepancy.

Misc breadcrumbs / commands copied for later:
- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')" &> ldlib-debug.txt
- sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced --since "2025-02-18" | sed -n '1,200p'
- docker run --gpus 'device=0' --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --rm -it my-serving-image:canary bash -c "LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 python serve.py --batch-size 24" > run.log 2>&1

Random notes:
- I saw one message inside container: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" while host nvidia-smi reported matching 535.x - this happens when toolkit lib comes first.
- MIG slices make fragmentation worse for large contiguous allocations; consider pre-allocating a big pinned buffer and sub-allocating if this pattern repeats.
- Consider switching to Triton for batching to control memory reuse more explicitly.

Short-term decision (owner: me):
- Roll out mitigation patch to reduce default batch-size to 12 for MIG slices and add a graceful fallback on allocation failure (fallback to smaller micro-batches).
- Continue repro effort for driver-version regression and collect artifacts for vendor escalation.

If anyone else is poking at this, see linked PR and INC above, and ping me on #eng-runtime (Ava) for live debugging.
